subject: maths
title: Year 1 Halves and Quarters
seo_title: Year 1 Halves and Quarters Worksheets: Half and Quarter of Shapes and Amounts (Free, with Answers)
standard_text: Recognise, find and name a half as one of two equal parts of an object, shape or quantity; recognise, find and name a quarter as one of four equal parts of an object, shape or quantity.
meta_desc: Free Year 1 halves and quarters worksheets for the National Curriculum: equal parts, a half and a quarter of shapes and objects, half and a quarter of an amount with counters and sweets, and real-life sharing problems. 100 picture questions with an answer key.
key_big: A half is 1 of 2 equal parts. A quarter is 1 of 4 equal parts.
key_sub: The parts must be the same size. To find half of 8, share 8 into 2 equal groups: 4 and 4. A half of something is bigger than a quarter of it.
body_html:
Equal parts

To share fairly, cut a shape into equal parts. Equal parts are all the same size.

A half

Cut a whole into 2 equal parts. Each part is a half. 2 halves make the whole.

A quarter

Cut a whole into 4 equal parts. Each part is a quarter. 4 quarters make the whole.

Equal partsEach part isWrittenThe whole
2a half122 halves
4a quarter144 quarters

Half of an amount

To find half of a number of things, share them into 2 equal groups. Count one group.

A quarter of an amount

To find a quarter, share them into 4 equal groups. Count one group.

A half is bigger than a quarter

Cut the same whole into more parts, and each part gets smaller.

Example 1

Find half of 10 biscuits.

Share 10 into 2 equal groups. Each group has 5. 5 + 5 = 10.

Answer: 5 biscuits

Example 2

Oliver shares a cake equally with 3 friends. How much does each one get?

Oliver and 3 friends are 4 people. 4 equal parts are quarters.

Answer: a quarter of the cake

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Calling 2 parts halves when they are not the same sizeCheck that the parts are equal first
Half of 8 is 2, or half of 8 is 16Share 8 into 2 equal groups: 4 and 4. Half of 8 is 4
Thinking a quarter is bigger than a half because 4 is more than 2More parts means smaller parts. A half is bigger
Counting the lines instead of the partsCount the parts: 2 lines can make 4 parts

faq.q: What fractions do children learn in Year 1?
faq.a: In Year 1, children learn to recognise, find and name a half and a quarter. They find halves and quarters of shapes, objects and small amounts, such as half of 8 sweets or a quarter of 12 counters.

faq.q: How do you find half of a number in Year 1?
faq.a: Share the objects into 2 equal groups and count one group. Half of 10 is 5, because 5 + 5 = 10.

faq.q: Is a quarter bigger than a half?
faq.a: No. A quarter is 1 of 4 equal parts and a half is 1 of 2 equal parts, so a half of the same thing is bigger. Folding a piece of paper in half and then in half again shows this well.

faq.q: What is a quarter in maths for children?
faq.a: A quarter is one of four equal parts of a whole. Four quarters make one whole, just like four slices of a pizza cut into quarters.

sets.title: Half and a quarter of an amount

items.q: Find half of 4 counters.
items.e: Share the 4 counters into 2 equal groups. Each group has 2. 2 + 2 = 4. So half of 4 is 2.

items.q: Find half of 6 sweets.
items.e: Share the 6 sweets into 2 equal groups. Each group has 3. 3 + 3 = 6. So half of 6 is 3.

items.q: Find half of 8 counters.
items.e: Share the 8 counters into 2 equal groups. Each group has 4. 4 + 4 = 8. So half of 8 is 4.

items.q: Find half of 10 sweets.
items.e: Share the 10 sweets into 2 equal groups. Each group has 5. 5 + 5 = 10. So half of 10 is 5.

items.q: Find half of 12 counters.
items.e: Share the 12 counters into 2 equal groups. Each group has 6. 6 + 6 = 12. So half of 12 is 6.

items.q: Find half of 14 sweets.
items.e: Share the 14 sweets into 2 equal groups. Each group has 7. 7 + 7 = 14. So half of 14 is 7.

items.q: Find half of 16 counters.
items.e: Share the 16 counters into 2 equal groups. Each group has 8. 8 + 8 = 16. So half of 16 is 8.

items.q: Find half of 20 sweets.
items.e: Share the 20 sweets into 2 equal groups. Each group has 10. 10 + 10 = 20. So half of 20 is 10.

items.q: Find a quarter of 4 sweets.
items.e: Share the 4 sweets into 4 equal groups. Each group has 1. 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 4. So a quarter of 4 is 1.

items.q: Find a quarter of 8 counters.
items.e: Share the 8 counters into 4 equal groups. Each group has 2. 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8. So a quarter of 8 is 2.

items.q: Find a quarter of 12 sweets.
items.e: Share the 12 sweets into 4 equal groups. Each group has 3. 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 12. So a quarter of 12 is 3.

items.q: Find a quarter of 16 sweets.
items.e: Share the 16 sweets into 4 equal groups. Each group has 4. 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 = 16. So a quarter of 16 is 4.

items.q: Find a quarter of 20 counters.
items.e: Share the 20 counters into 4 equal groups. Each group has 5. 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 20. So a quarter of 20 is 5.

items.q: What part of the counters is in the green box?
items.e: There are 6 counters in 2 equal groups of 3. 1 group is green. So the green group is half of the counters.

items.q: What part of the sweets is in the green box?
items.e: There are 16 sweets in 2 equal groups of 8. 1 group is green. So the green group is half of the sweets.

items.q: What part of the sweets is in the green box?
items.e: There are 12 sweets in 4 equal groups of 3. 1 group is green. So the green group is a quarter of the sweets.

items.q: What part of the counters is in the green box?
items.e: There are 8 counters in 4 equal groups of 2. 1 group is green. So the green group is a quarter of the counters.

items.q: What part of the counters is in the green box?
items.e: There are 2 groups, but one has 5 and one has 3. They are not equal, so the green group is not a half.

items.q: 12 counters are in 3 equal groups. Is the green box a quarter?
items.e: A quarter is 1 of 4 equal groups. Here there are only 3 groups. There are 4 counters in the box, but that does not make it a quarter.

items.q: Freya and Jack share 10 sweets. Freya gets 6. Jack gets 4. Do they each get half?
items.e: Half of 10 is 5. Halves are equal: 5 and 5. 6 and 4 are not equal.

items.q: Ruby eats the green slice of pizza. How much of the pizza does she eat?
items.e: The pizza has 4 equal slices. Ruby eats 1 of them. That is a quarter.

items.q: Harry has the green part of the cake. How much does he have?
items.e: The cake has 2 equal parts. Harry has 1 of them. That is a half.

items.q: Alfie breaks this chocolate bar in half. How many squares are in each half?
items.e: The bar has 8 squares. Half of 8 is 4, because 4 + 4 = 8.

items.q: Arjun has these sweets. He gives half to Maya. How many sweets does Maya get?
items.e: There are 18 sweets. Share them into 2 equal groups. 9 + 9 = 18. Maya gets 9.

items.q: Freya has half of a cake. Leo has a quarter of the same cake. Who has more?
items.e: A half is 1 of 2 equal parts. A quarter is 1 of 4 equal parts. 4 parts are smaller. So Freya has more.

items.q: Which is bigger: half of an orange or a quarter of the same orange?
items.e: 4 is more than 2, but more parts means smaller parts. So a half is bigger.

items.q: Amelia shares a pizza equally with 1 friend. How much does each one get?
items.e: Amelia and 1 friend are 2 people. 2 equal parts are halves. Each one gets a half.

items.q: Oliver shares a cake equally with 3 friends. How much does each one get?
items.e: Oliver and 3 friends are 4 people. 4 equal parts are quarters. Do not forget to count Oliver.

items.q: Isla and Noah share 10 grapes equally. How many grapes does each one get?
items.e: Share 10 into 2 equal groups. 5 + 5 = 10. Each one gets 5.

items.q: 4 friends share 8 strawberries equally. How many does each friend get?
items.e: Share 8 into 4 equal groups. 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8. A quarter of 8 is 2.

items.q: There are 14 children in a group. Half of them play football. How many play football?
items.e: Half of 14 is 7, because 7 + 7 = 14.

items.q: A box has 16 crayons. A quarter of them are red. How many are red?
items.e: Share 16 into 4 equal groups. 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 = 16. A quarter of 16 is 4.

items.q: Evie shares 12 stickers equally with her friend. How many does each one get?
items.e: 2 people share. Half of 12 is 6, because 6 + 6 = 12.

items.q: Jack has 6 biscuits. He gives half of them to Zara. How many does Jack have left?
items.e: Half of 6 is 3. Jack gives 3 away, so he has 3 left.

items.q: Kai cuts a sandwich into 2 parts. One is big and one is small. Is each part a half?
items.e: Halves must be the same size. A big part and a small part are not halves.

items.q: Ava folds some paper in half. Then she folds it in half again. She opens it. How many equal parts are there?
items.e: 2 folds that cross make 4 equal parts. They are quarters.

items.q: Mohammed eats half of a pizza. Then he eats the other half. How much does he eat?
items.e: 2 halves make 1 whole. Mohammed eats the whole pizza.

items.q: Lily cuts a cake into quarters. She eats 1 quarter. How many quarters are left?
items.e: The whole cake is 4 quarters. Lily eats 1. 4 − 1 = 3 quarters are left.

items.q: Poppy cuts an apple into quarters. How many pieces does she have?
items.e: Quarters means 4 equal pieces.

items.q: Charlie wants to cut a cake in half. Where should he cut?
items.e: A cut down the middle makes 2 equal parts. A cut near one end makes a big part and a small part.
